decision.question: how to tell a real `node server.js`/`node Server/run.js` invocation apart from the string merely appearing as someone else's argument
options: one big regex matching the strings anywhere in the command
split into shell segments, find the `node` token, take its first non-flag argument, test that
decision.chose: split into shell segments, find the `node` token, take its first non-flag argument, test that
decision.why: a single regex would also fire on `node merge.mjs --log server.js.log` or a commit message that happens to mention the words; token scanning only fires when `server.js`/`Server/run.js` is the actual script node is about to run. The Start-Process/-ArgumentList form is checked against the raw (unstripped) command instead, since its script path usually sits inside the quoted argument list that the quote-stripping used for the other checks would blank out.
